examples.en: I saw old photos in Grandma's album.
I ran into an old friend on the street.
There are old palaces in Seoul.
I met an old friend after a long time.

examples.ko: 옛 사진을 보면 어릴 때가 생각나요.
examples.en: Looking at old photos reminds me of my childhood.

explain: “옛”은 꼭 명사 앞에 와요. “옛 친구”처럼요. 따로 쓰는 말은 “옛날”이에요: “옛날에는…”.

dict_examples.en: The hometown I visited ten years later was just as it used to be.

explain_en: 옛 always comes right before a noun, like 옛 친구. The word you can use alone is 옛날: “옛날에는…” (in the old days…).

examples.ko: 할머니 앨범에는 옛 사진이 많이 있어요.
examples.en: Grandma's album has lots of old photos in it.
We made an album out of our wedding photos.

examples.ko: 앨범 첫 장에 우리 가족 사진이 있어요.
examples.en: The first page of the album has our family photo.

examples.ko: 앨범을 넘기면서 어릴 때 이야기를 했어요.
examples.en: We talked about our childhood as we flipped through the album.

examples.ko: 친구가 여행 사진으로 앨범을 만들어 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend made an album from our trip photos for me.

explain: 앨범은 가수의 음반도 뜻해요. “새 앨범이 나왔어요”처럼 써요. 문장을 보면 어느 뜻인지 알 수 있어요.

dict_examples.en: I bought a few albums by my favorite singer.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 앨범 also means a singer's music album: 새 앨범이 나왔어요. The sentence tells you which meaning is meant.

examples.en: I won a prize at a Korean language contest.
That film won a major award.

examples.ko: 수학 시험에서 일 등을 해서 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: I came first in the math test and won a prize.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 노래 대회에서 상을 받은 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: There's a classmate in our class who won a prize at a singing contest.

examples.ko: 상을 받으면 가족하고 같이 저녁을 먹을 거예요.
examples.en: If I win the prize, I'll have dinner with my family.

explain: “상을 받다”는 가장 기본이에요. 말할 때는 “상을 타다”도 많이 써요. “상 탔어요!”라고 해요.
explain_en: “상을 받다” is the standard phrase. In speech, “상을 타다” is also common: “상 탔어요!”

dis.h: award for achievement or winning a contest

p.n: 경품 would mean a free gift won by draw, not an award earned by skill.

examples.ko: 이건 제가 한국에서 받은 첫 상이에요.
examples.en: This is the first prize I've won in Korea.
I bought my parents a gift with my first paycheck.
In the first Korean class, I learned greetings.

examples.ko: 첫 번째 문제는 쉽고 두 번째 문제는 어려워요.
examples.en: The first question is easy and the second one is hard.
My first job in Korea was at a small company.

explain: “첫”은 꼭 명사 앞에 와요: 첫 수업, 첫 직장. “처음”은 따로 쓸 수 있어요: “처음 만났어요”.

phrases.en: to fall in love at first sight
phrases.nuance_en: used when you fall for someone the moment you see them
phrases.en_equiv: to fall in love at first sight

examples.en: I bought flowers as a birthday present for my friend.
What would be a good birthday present for my mother?
Please gift-wrap it.
I got a birthday present and felt happy.
Who are you going to give this present to?

explain_en: To an elder you say 선물을 드려요; to a friend, 선물을 줘요.

examples.en: I wrote down my memories of that day in my notebook.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 기억이 잘 안 나요.
examples.en: I don't remember much from when I was little.
I still remember that trip clearly.

examples.ko: 비밀번호가 기억이 안 나서 새로 만들었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't remember the password, so I made a new one.

examples.ko: 친구하고 같이 간 여행은 좋은 기억이에요.
examples.en: The trip I went on with my friend is a good memory.

explain: “기억나요”는 저절로 생각이 날 때 써요. “기억해요”는 잊지 않고 알고 있을 때 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 잘 안 나는 기억을 천천히 떠올리다
phrases.nuance_en: used when you slowly try to recall a memory that is hard to bring back

explain_en: 기억나요 is for when something comes to mind by itself. 기억해요 is for keeping something in mind and not forgetting.

p.n: 추억 adds a warm, nostalgic feeling. 기억 is neutral.

examples.en: I forgot the words I learned yesterday.
I felt terrible because I forgot my friend's birthday.
I forgot my password, so I couldn't log in.
I haven't forgotten my friends back home.

examples.ko: 그날 본 노을은 평생 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can never forget the sunset I saw that day.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 ‘잊어버렸어요’나 ‘깜빡했어요’도 많이 써요. ‘잊다’는 노래 가사나 글에서도 자주 보여요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to forget the spelling of an English word
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 본 지 오래된 영화라서 그 제목을 잊었다.
dict_examples.en: It's a movie I saw long ago, so I forgot its title.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: In everyday talk, 잊어버렸어요 and 깜빡했어요 are also very common. 잊다 shows up a lot in song lyrics and writing too.

dis.h: neutral; also letting go of memories, feelings

p.n: 잊어버리다 stresses that it is completely gone from memory.

en: partner (in a pair), one of a pair

examples.en: My partner in class is Ben.
One of my socks is missing.

examples.ko: 오늘은 짝하고 같이 대화 연습을 해요.
examples.en: Today we practice conversation with a partner.
I can't find one of my earrings anywhere.
We switched partners and asked and answered questions.

explain: ‘짝’은 두 개가 한 쌍일 때 그중 하나예요. 신발 한 켤레는 두 개이고, 신발 한 짝은 한 개예요.

dict_examples.ko: 이 시는 앞과 뒤의 글귀가 짝을 이루어 배치되어 있다.
dict_examples.en: In this poem, the lines at the front and back are arranged as pairs.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 짝 is one of a pair. A pair of shoes is 한 켤레 (two shoes); one single shoe is 한 짝.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 심은 나무가 집 앞에 있어요.
examples.en: There's a tree my grandfather planted in front of the house.
In spring I planted flowers in the yard.

examples.ko: 학교 앞에 새로 심은 나무가 아직 작아요.
examples.en: The tree newly planted in front of the school is still small.
On the weekend I planted lettuce with my family.
What did you plant? — Chili peppers and perilla.

explain: 심은 것을 땅에서 뽑을 때는 ‘뽑다’, 열매나 꽃을 가지에서 딸 때는 ‘따다’를 써요.

phrases.ko: 콩 심은 데 콩 나고 팥 심은 데 팥 난다
phrases.example: 열심히 공부하니까 성적이 올랐네요. 콩 심은 데 콩 나죠.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 일에 맞는 결과가 나온다는 속담
phrases.nuance_en: a proverb saying that results match what you put in

explain_en: To pull up something you planted, use 뽑다. To pick fruit or flowers from a branch, use 따다.

en: to raise (an animal), to grow (a plant)

examples.en: Our family is raising a puppy.
I grow tomatoes on the balcony.
I kept a hamster when I was little.
I want to grow my hair out and tie it back.
Raising a child is not easy.

explain: 말할 때는 ‘키우다’도 많이 써요. 강아지와 화분은 둘 다 돼요. 머리·수염·습관은 ‘기르다’가 더 자연스러워요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 체력을 기르기 위해 매일 운동을 한다.
dict_examples.en: He exercises every day to build up his stamina.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그들은 단결 정신을 기르고 강인한 체력을 연마하였다.
dict_examples.en: They developed a spirit of unity and honed strong physical strength.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 매일 조금씩 읽으면서 한국어 실력을 길러요.
dict_examples.en: I build my Korean skills by reading a little every day.
dict_examples.src: AI 생성 · 검수

explain_en: In speech, 키우다 is also very common, and both work for pets and plants. For hair, a beard or a habit, 기르다 sounds more natural.

dis.h: raise pets or plants; grow hair, beard

p.n: Same meaning. 키우다 is the everyday word. 기르다 sounds slightly more formal. Only 기르다 is used for growing hair or a beard.

en: to part, to say goodbye; to break up

examples.en: I said goodbye to my friend in front of the station.

examples.ko: 여자 친구하고 헤어져서 요즘 많이 힘들어요.
examples.en: I broke up with my girlfriend, so things are hard right now.
After the meal we said goodbye in front of the subway station.
Are you still together? — No, we broke up last month.
We took a photo before parting from my friends.

explain: ‘우리 헤어졌어요’처럼 사람 이름 없이 말하면 연인과 끝났다는 뜻일 때가 많아요. 친구와 인사하고 갈라질 때도 같은 말을 써요.

dict_examples.en: I parted from my group and came home.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 모임이 끝나고 친구들과 헤어지고 나니 무척 섭섭하였다.
dict_examples.en: After the gathering ended and I said goodbye to my friends, I felt very sad.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 주방 쪽으로 걸어가는 하명과 헤어져 지혜는 분장실로 갔다.
dict_examples.en: Parting from Hamyeong, who was walking toward the kitchen, Jihye went to the dressing room.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 어머니는 남문 밖까지 따라나오며 차마 아들, 며느리와 헤어지기가 마음에 아픈지, 훌쩍훌쩍 눈물 바람을 하였다.
dict_examples.en: Mother followed them out beyond the south gate, sobbing, as if it pained her to part from her son and daughter-in-law.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Said alone like ‘우리 헤어졌어요’, it often means a couple broke up. The same word is also used when friends simply part ways.

examples.en: I woke up at five in the morning.
I woke up in the night because of the thunder.
I woke up at dawn because I was thirsty.
The baby woke up in the middle of the night and cried.

examples.ko: 잘 잤어요? — 아니요, 두 번이나 깼어요.
examples.en: Did you sleep well? — No, I woke up twice.

explain: ‘깨다’는 잠에서 눈이 떠지는 것이고, ‘일어나다’는 자리에서 몸을 일으키는 거예요. 새벽에 깼어도 바로 일어나지 않을 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 물을 많이 마시니까 술이 좀 깼어요.
phrases.nuance_en: used when you recover from being drunk

explain_en: 깨다 is when your eyes open and sleep ends; 일어나다 is getting up out of bed. You can 깨다 at dawn and still not 일어나다.

dis.h: stop sleeping, often because of noise

p.n: Waking up versus actually getting out of bed.

examples.en: I bought two outfits.

examples.ko: 여행 가방에 옷을 세 벌 넣었어요.
examples.en: I packed three outfits in my suitcase.

examples.ko: 친구 결혼식에 입으려고 한복 한 벌을 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I rented a hanbok to wear to my friend's wedding.

examples.ko: 면접 때문에 양복 한 벌을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a suit because of a job interview.

examples.ko: 코트가 몇 벌 있어요? — 두 벌 있어요.
examples.en: How many coats do you have? — I have two.

explain: 옷은 ‘벌’, 신발과 양말은 ‘켤레’로 세요. 양복이나 잠옷처럼 윗옷과 바지가 한 세트면 한 벌이에요.

dict_examples.ko: 경심이와 친구는 동대문 시장에 가서 경심이의 옷을 두어 벌 샀다.
dict_examples.en: Gyeongsim and her friend went to Dongdaemun Market and bought a couple of outfits for Gyeongsim.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 결혼식 때 양복이나 한 벌 해 주고 좋은 시계나 사 주면 되지.
dict_examples.en: For the wedding, we can just get him a suit and buy him a nice watch.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Clothes are counted with 벌; shoes and socks use 켤레. A suit or pajamas, where top and bottom come as a set, count as one 벌.

examples.en: That dog died last winter.

examples.ko: 물을 안 줘서 화분의 꽃이 죽었어요.
examples.en: I didn't water it, so the flower in the pot died.

examples.ko: 겨울에 너무 추워서 정원의 나무가 죽었어요.
examples.en: It was so cold in winter that the tree in the garden died.
The fish died, and the child cried a lot.
A dead tree has no leaves.

explain: 사람이 세상을 떠났을 때는 보통 ‘돌아가셨어요’라고 말해요. ‘죽었어요’는 동물이나 식물에 많이 써요.

phrases.en: to be dying of ~, so ~ (strong exaggeration)
phrases.nuance_en: a strong exaggeration meaning something is extremely intense, as in 더워 죽겠다
phrases.en_equiv: to be dying of ~, so ~ (strong exaggeration)

phrases.nuance_en: used when you do something with all your strength, as if your life depended on it

explain_en: When a person has passed away, people usually say 돌아가셨어요. 죽었어요 is more common for animals and plants.

p.n: 숨지다 sounds like a news report; 죽다 is plain and direct.

examples.en: Our dog has gotten old, too.
My parents have gotten a lot older.

examples.ko: 늙기 전에 세계 여행을 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to travel the world before I get old.

examples.ko: 우리 고양이가 늙어서 하루 종일 자요.
examples.en: Our cat is old now and sleeps all day.
I made porridge with ripe pumpkin.

explain: 사람에게 ‘늙었어요’라고 바로 말하면 조금 무례하게 들려요. 부드럽게 말할 때는 ‘나이가 들다’를 써요.

phrases.example: 할아버지는 춤 수업도 들으세요. 몸은 늙어도 마음은 청춘이에요.
phrases.en: Old in body, young at heart.
phrases.nuance_en: used about an older person who still feels young inside
phrases.en_equiv: Old in body, young at heart.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The cucumber is overripe, so I can't eat it as is.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Telling a person ‘늙었어요’ directly can sound a bit rude. For a softer way, say 나이가 들다.
